svg.title: The Lantern and the Shade
svg.desc: Cross-section through the spin axis: the hole and disk at the centre, the Lantern shell at 0.82 pc, hotter over the poles, and the Shade's rafts from 0.9 to 1.25 pc, fed by microwave beams.
svg.text: The Lantern and the Shade
Cut through the hole's spin axis. Radii to scale; the hole, disk and rafts are not.
spin axis
0.5 pc ≈ 1.6 light-years
The Lantern, ~0.82 pc out
A closed shell of hovering collectors, ~50,000 M☉.
Catches ~98% of the disk's light; held up mostly
by infrared trapped inside it. Nobody lives there.
Sgr A* and its disk
4.3 × 10⁶ M☉, fed at 30% of Eddington. The disk
(4–40 AU) is drawn thousands of times too big.
The Shade, 0.9–1.25 pc
~1.27 × 10³³ people in rafts on crossing orbits
of ~39,000 years, passing at 100–300 km/s.
Microwave beams cross the gap
~75% from transmitter to rectenna. Power is
booked a year ahead: 3 months to 1.4 years by light.
The disk shines toward its poles
Latitude, and the Lantern's flux against its average
Polar skins run ~530 K, the belt's much cooler.
The frontier's mines are 100–200 pc out, far off the page.
